cases.command: echo k > /data2/xm_keep && ln -s /data2/xm_keep /data2/xm_lk && cp -l --remove-destination /data/a.txt /data2/xm_lk; echo rc=$?; cat /data2/xm_keep; test -L /data2/xm_lk || echo gone; rm /data2/xm_keep

expect.stderr: cp: cannot create hard link '/data2/xm_lk' to '/data/a.txt': Invalid cross-device link

cases.note: coreutils 9.7 over tmpfs mounts: --remove-destination removes the link standing at the name, never what it leads to. The refusal used to remove /data2/xm_keep and leave the link.

cases.command: mkdir /data2/xm_real /data2/xm_out && echo f > /data2/xm_real/file && ln -s file /data2/xm_real/l && ln -s /data2/xm_real /data/xm_alias && cp -Pl /data/xm_alias/l /data/a.txt /data2/xm_out; echo rc=$?; readlink /data2/xm_out/l; rm -r /data2/xm_real /data2/xm_out /data/xm_alias

expect.stderr: cp: cannot create hard link '/data2/xm_out/a.txt' to '/data/a.txt': Invalid cross-device link

cases.note: coreutils 9.7 over tmpfs mounts: the link typed under /data stands on /data2 once the alias above it is followed, so link(2) makes it; only a.txt is on the other device.
